1507: Ismail takes Diyarbakir. 'In 1507, he conquered Diyarbakir.' The page does not name the holder; the Aq Qoyunlu shape of 1507-1511 reaches 37.96 E.

1508: Baghdad falls and the Aq Qoyunlu end. 'The same year, Ismail and Husayn Beg Shamlu seized Baghdad, putting an end to the Aq Qoyunlu.' The Safavid Iran page says 1509 ('the capture of Baghdad by Ismail I in 1509'); Cliopatria's Safavid shape has Iraq from 1507 and its Aq Qoyunlu row runs to 1511.

region.text: Herat, as well as other parts of Khorasan

ledger.note: 1510: Ismail takes Khorasan from the Uzbeks. 'Herat, as well as other parts of Khorasan, in 1510'; 'by 1511, the Uzbeks in the north-east, led by their Khan Muhammad Shaybani, were driven far to the north' (Muhammad Shaybani was killed at the Battle of Merv in 1510 per the Ismail I page).

region.text: the Georgian kingdoms of Kartli and Kakheti

ledger.note: By 1510 Kartli is a Safavid vassal. The page says that by 1510 Ismail had conquered 'the whole of Iran (including Shirvan)' and made the Georgian kingdoms of Kartli and Kakheti his vassals; the year is the page's 'by 1510'.
By 1510 Kakheti is a Safavid vassal (same sentence as Kartli).
1514: Selim I defeats Ismail at Chaldiran. 'Selim I eventually defeated Ismail at the Battle of Chaldiran in 1514' and 'Selim entered the Iranian capital of Tabriz in triumph on September 5'.
1514: Selim leaves Tabriz. The page is silent on the Ottoman withdrawal; the contest is closed in the same year because Tabriz stays Safavid (Tahmasp I page: Tabriz is occupied again only in 1534).

union.text: the Jazira, Armenian Highlands and Syria cells inside the Ottoman shapes of 1534 and 1540, Iraq excluded

region.text: Eastern Anatolia and Upper Mesopotamia, and the Syrian lands drawn in the Safavid shapes (Ottoman shapes of 1516, 1534 and 1540)

ledger.note: 1516: Eastern Anatolia and Upper Mesopotamia pass to the Ottomans. The page says only that after Chaldiran the Ottomans 'managed to annex for the first time Eastern Anatolia and parts of Mesopotamia'; the year is bridged from Cliopatria's Ottoman shape, which grows east to 44.03 E in 1516. [fx-26, F086: region widened from the Ottoman 1516 shape to the Jazira, Armenian Highlands and Syria cells in the Ottoman shapes of 1534 and 1540 (Iraq excluded: Baghdad and the south stay Safavid to 1534-1555). Battle of Chaldiran page: 'the Ottomans annexed Eastern Anatolia and Upper Mesopotamia from Safavid Iran', 'these areas changed hands several times over the following decades' and the hold was settled only by the Peace of Amasya (1555); Syria passed from the Mamluks at Marj Dabiq (August 1516).]

region.text: the Khorasan borderlands taken by the Uzbeks

ledger.note: 1524: the Uzbeks overrun the Khorasan borderlands. 'While the civil war was ongoing among the Qizilbash, the Uzbeks under Ubayd Allah Khan conquered the borderlands'; a battle between Tahmasp and Ubayd Allah Khan is dated 24 September 1524. The page gives the year by its context.

region.text: Astarabad, Tus and the Khorasan marches

ledger.note: 1528: Tahmasp beats the Uzbeks at Jam. 'In 1528, Ubayd reconquered Astarabad and Tus and besieged Herat', 'that year, the Uzbeks captured Herat', but 'at the age of fourteen, he defeated the Uzbeks in the Battle of Jam by using artillery'. Cliopatria's shape recovers in 1529.

region.text: Baghdad and the Shia cities such as Najaf

ledger.note: 1534: Baghdad passes to Suleiman. 'Suleiman peacefully conquered Baghdad and Shia cities such as Najaf'; the page gives no separate year (it follows the Tabriz occupation of 1534), and Suleiman kept Baghdad when he 'lost all his gains' elsewhere by the end of 1535.
1534: the Ottomans occupy Tabriz. 'Suleiman sent his grand vizier, Ibrahim Pasha, to occupy Tabriz in July 1534 and joined him two months later.'
1535: the Ottomans leave Tabriz. 'Suleiman was forced to retreat to Constantinople at the end of 1535 after losing all his gains except Baghdad.'
1539: Shirvan is annexed. No page opened dates the annexation: Cliopatria's Shirvan row ends in 1539 and the Safavid shape grows to 41.98 N in 1540 (confidence 1).
1539: Safavid annexation of Shirvan. Bridged from the Cliopatria rows (see the vassal_end of the same year); the Ismail I page already calls Shirvan conquered by 1510.
1548: a second Ottoman invasion. 'The new invasion sought the quick capture of Tabriz in July 1548'; 'by the fall of 1549 the remaining Ottoman forces retreated'.
1549: the Ottomans retreat. 'By the fall of 1549 the remaining Ottoman forces retreated.'
1555: Tahmasp moves the court from Tabriz to Qazvin. 'In 1555, Shah Tahmasp transferred the capital from Tabriz to Qazvin.'
1555: the Peace of Amasya. 'Tahmasp recognised Ottoman sovereignty in Mesopotamia and much of Kurdistan'; 'eastern Georgia remained in Iranian hands and western Georgia was ruled by the Turks'.
1558: Tahmasp retakes Kandahar. He 'began the first Safavid expedition to Kandahar in 1558, after the death of Humayun, and reconquered the city'.

region.text: the Caucasus and Azerbaijan, the zone of the war of 1578-1590

ledger.note: 1578: the Ottoman-Safavid war of Murad III begins. The war table lists 'Murad III vs. Mohammad Khodabanda / Abbas I, 1578-1590'; the pages opened give no campaign dates before the treaty.

1587: Hamadan and Luristan fall to the Ottomans. 'Cigalazade Yusuf Sinan Pasha managed to take Luristan and Hamadan' (Ottoman-Safavid War 1578-1590 page, dated 1587); Tabriz had been taken in 1585. The Treaty of Constantinople (21 March 1590) cedes Luristan and Kurdistan again (the loss of 1590). Kermanshah, Kordestan and Khuzestan are not dated before 1590 on the page and stay Safavid until then. Mirror: ottoman-empire gain of 1587. Added by fx-26 (F086): the 1588 Ottoman shape draws these lands and the Safavid state still held them.
1589: the Uzbeks take Herat. The page has the Uzbeks take Herat and slaughter its population, placed before Murshid Quli Khan's assassination on 23 July 1589.

region.text: Mashhad and the rest of Khorasan, Uzbek-held until Abbas's campaign of 1598

ledger.note: Mashhad falls to the Uzbeks. The page is silent on when; it has Abbas recapture Mashhad in April 1598 (paraphrase of the page's table), so the loss is bridged to 1589, the year of Herat.

region.text: Azerbaijan, Karabagh, Shirvan, Dagestan, parts of Georgia, Lorestan, Kurdistan, and Tabriz

ledger.note: 1590: the Treaty of Constantinople. Abbas made what the page calls a 'humiliating peace treaty', ceding Azerbaijan, Karabagh, Shirvan, Dagestan, parts of Georgia, Lorestan, Kurdistan and Tabriz to the Ottomans (paraphrase of the list).
1590: the war of 1578-1590 ends with the Treaty of Constantinople (Ottoman-Persian Wars page: 'Constantinople (1590)').

region.text: Kandahar, which 'capitulated without resistance on 18 April 1595'

ledger.note: 18 April 1595: Kandahar passes to the Mughals. 'The city capitulated without resistance on 18 April 1595, and the ruler Mozaffar-Hosayn Mirza joined Akbar's court'; the page calls him the Safavid prince and governor of Kandahar who agreed to defect. The Abbas I page dates the seizure earlier: 'In 1590, profiting from the confusion in Iran, Humayun's successor Akbar seized Kandahar'; the Akbar page has no 1590, names the day and is the mirror of mughal-empire /ledger/58, so 1595 is followed. Added after review: the dossier had Kandahar gained in 1558 and again in 1622 with no loss between.
1598: Abbas I moves the capital from Qazvin to Isfahan. The Abbas I page has him move the capital in 1598 (paraphrase); Safavid Iran infobox: 'Isfahan (1598-1736)'.
1598: Abbas retakes Mashhad. The page's first campaign of Abbas against the Uzbeks recaptured Mashhad in April 1598 (paraphrase).

1598-1599: Herat returns. The Abbas I page has a battle against the Uzbeks in the Herat area on 9 August 1598 and Abbas holding Herat and Mashhad in 1599 (paraphrase); it gives no separate date for the city.
1599: Abbas advances to Balkh. Paraphrase of the page: holding Herat and Mashhad, he advanced as far as Balkh, which was lost again in 1602.
1602: Balkh is lost again (paraphrase of the Abbas I page).

1602: Bahrain is taken from the Portuguese. Abbas 'dislodge[d] the Portuguese from Bahrain (1602)'; the Abbas I page has an Iranian army under Imam Quli Khan expelling them. The Portuguese holdings were under the Iberian Union in these years (iberian-union has a Cliopatria row 1582-1639).
1603: Abbas goes on the offensive. 'In 1603 Abbas launched an offensive that retook Tabriz, Azerbaijan and Georgia in the same year.' Table of wars: 'Ahmed I vs Abbas I, 1603-1612'.
1603: Tabriz, Azerbaijan and Georgia retaken (quote above); the Abbas I page gives Tabriz without a year, Yerevan in June 1604.
1604: Yerevan falls to Abbas in June 1604, and he won a decisive victory over the Ottomans at Sufiyan near Tabriz on 6 November 1605 (paraphrase of the Abbas I page).

June 1606: Abbas I liberates Ganja, Baku, Shirvan and Shamakhi (paraphrase of the page's list; mirror ottoman-empire /ledger/100). This returns part of what the 1590 treaty gave away. Karabakh, which the page does not name for 1606, is entered with the treaty of 1612. Added after review.

region.text: Daghestan, Karabakh, Lorestan and the rest of Azerbaijan, regained with the Treaty of Nasuh Pasha

ledger.note: 20 November 1612: the Treaty of Nasuh Pasha. Infobox territorial changes: 'Safavids regain control over the territories ceded in 1590 to the Ottomans' and 'Azerbaijan, Georgia, Erivan Province, Daghestan, Shirvan, Karabakh, Lorestan, and Khuzestan'; the article says the treaty secured the 1555 borders of the Peace of Amasya. Georgia, Yerevan and Shirvan are entered under 1603, 1604 and 1606; Daghestan, Karabakh and Lorestan are named by the infobox; West Azarbaijan is my reading of 'Azerbaijan' (the 1603 gain names only East Azarbaijan and Tabriz). Kurdistan, ceded in 1590, is not on the infobox list and the Amasya frontier left the Kurdish marches with the Ottomans, so it is not entered; Khuzestan was not ceded in 1590 on the Abbas I page (a page oddity). The Abbas I page: 'By the end of the 1603-1618 Ottoman War, Abbas had regained possession over South Caucasus and Dagestan' (mirror ottoman-empire /ledger/102). Added after review.

20 November 1612: the Treaty of Nasuh Pasha ends the war of 1603-1612 (page infobox: '26 September 1603 - 20 November 1612', result Safavid victory). The Abbas I page: 'The Persian victory was recognised in the Treaty of Nasuh Pasha in 1612', restoring suzerainty over most of the Caucasus (paraphrase).
1622: Hormuz is retaken. 'In 1622 four of its [the English East India Company's] ships helped Abbas retake Hormuz from the Portuguese.'

region.text: Kandahar, which 'fell on 22 June' after a siege that began on 20 May

ledger.note: 22 June 1622: Abbas retakes Kandahar from the Mughals. The Mughal-Persian wars page: Abbas 'arrived on 20 May and immediately began the siege' and 'after a 45-day siege the city fell on 22 June'; the sentence carries no year and the page labels the war 'The Mughal-Safavid war of 1622-1623'. The year 1622 is the Abbas I page's: 'Abbas realized that he needed just a lightning raid to take back the far easternmost town of Kandahar in 1622.' The matching loss is mughal-empire /ledger/67 (June 1622). The Mughal capture that this reverses is the 18 April 1595 loss above.

1624: the Persians take Baghdad. 'The Persians besieged Baghdad and took it on 14 January 1624' (Bakr Subashi had held it for the Ottomans from 1621). The Abbas I page says 1623 'under the guise of a pilgrimage'; the war table has Murad IV vs Abbas I and Safi, 1623-1639.
1625: the Ottoman army besieges Baghdad. Hafiz Ahmed Pasha's army 'invested it in November on three sides'; it 'lifted the siege and withdrew to Mosul' on 4 July 1626.
1626: the siege of Baghdad is lifted (4 July).
1635: the Ottomans take Revan. 'The Ottomans took Revan (on 8 August) and plundered Tabriz.'
1636: Shah Safi retakes Revan. 'In the spring of the next year, Shah Safi retook Revan and defeated an Ottoman army.'

region.text: Kandahar, handed over by the Persian commander Ali Mardan Khan

ledger.note: 1638: Ali Mardan Khan hands Kandahar to Shah Jahan. The page has Shah Jahan take Kandahar in 1638, having 'negotiated the surrender from the Persian commander' Ali Mardan Khan, a Kurdish turncoat (the Mughal-Persian wars page: Ali Mardan Khan 'surrendered the keys of Kandahar to the Mughals' in the Mughal-Safavid war of 1638). Neither page gives a month. Mirror: mughal-empire /ledger/73. Added after review.
1638: Murad IV besieges Baghdad. 'The city fell in December after a siege of 39 days.'
1638: Baghdad falls to Murad IV. The Safavid Iran page: 'lost it again to Murad IV in 1638'.
1639: the Treaty of Zuhab ends the war of 1623-1639 'concluded on 17 May 1639'.
1639: Iraq is ceded for good. Mesopotamia 'was thereby irrevocably lost'; 'the frontier postulated by the treaty remains to this day the western border of Iran with Iraq and Turkey'.

22 February 1649: the war for Kandahar opens with the Safavid capture. Shah Abbas II marched from Isfahan on 4 April 1648, took Bust, began the siege of Kandahar on 28 December 1648 and the city fell after a brief siege on 22 February 1649 (page, infobox dates 28 December 1648 - 29 September 1653). The contest is dated to the capture, as in mughal-empire /ledger/79. Added after review.
22 February 1649: Kandahar is retaken from the Mughals. Infobox territorial changes: 'Kandahar falls again to the Safavids.' Mirror: mughal-empire /ledger/80. Added after review.

region.text: Kandahar, abandoned by the Mughals on 29 September 1653

ledger.note: 29 September 1653: the Mughals 'finally gave up all attempts to recover Kandahar'. The page lists the failed attempts of 1651 (stopped by winter), 1652 (Aurangzeb, who abandoned the campaign after two months with Uzbek raids on his supplies) and 1653 (Dara Shikoh, five-month siege); infobox result: Safavid victory. Mirror: mughal-empire /ledger/81. Added after review.

region.text: the Kandahar oasis the Hotaki hold from 21 April 1709 (their 1709 shape, 17 cells), not the whole province

ledger.note: 1709: Mirwais Hotak rises at Kandahar. 'Mirwais and his men ambushed Gurgin Khan on 21 April and killed him.' Cliopatria's Safavid shape keeps Kandahar to 1712. [fx-44, R077: the loss had the whole province of Kandahar (197 cells) but the Hotaki found and keyframe hold only the oasis, so the Hotaki snap released 180 cells to nobody. Restricted to the Hotaki 1709 shape; the rest of the province stays Safavid until 1712-13: the Hotak dynasty page, 'With this, Mirwais was able to extend his control over the entire province of Kandahar', follows the failed Persian expedition of 1712 and gives no date.]

region.text: central Persia between Gulnabad and Isfahan

ledger.note: 1722: the Hotaki invade Persia. Mahmud's Afghan army, 'after defeating the Persian army at the Battle of Gulnabad on 8 March 1722' and besieged Isfahan for about six months.

region.text: Isfahan and central Persia, the land Cliopatria gives the Hotaki in 1727-1733

ledger.note: 23 October 1722: Isfahan falls. 'Sultan Husayn abdicated and acknowledged Mahmud as the new Shah of Persia.' The page names Isfahan; the extent of Hotaki rule is taken from the Cliopatria Hotaki shape (my reading).

10 November 1722: Tahmasp II proclaims himself shah at Qazvin. 'On 10 November 1722 he declared himself shah and assumed the regnal name of Tahmasp II.' The capital dot moves to Qazvin until the Hotaki are driven out.

region.text: Derbent, Baku and the surrounding lands, plus the provinces of Gilan, Shirvan, Mazandaran, and Astarabad

ledger.note: 1723: the Treaty of Saint Petersburg. Under it Safavid Iran ceded Derbent, Baku and surrounding lands, plus the provinces of Gilan, Shirvan, Mazandaran and Astarabad, to Russia (Tahmasp II page, paraphrase); Peter the Great had declared war in June 1722.

region.text: large parts of Iranian Azerbaijan with Ardabil and Tabriz, Hamadan, Kermanshah and much of Transcaucasia

ledger.note: 1724: the Ottomans and Russia partition the Safavid periphery. The Treaty of Constantinople (signed 12 June 1724) gave 'the lands on the west' to the Ottomans and the Caspian lands east of the Kura-Aras confluence to Russia; Tahmasp II was not a party.

region.text: Kartli, passing to the Ottomans with 'much of Transcaucasia' under the Treaty of Constantinople

ledger.note: 1724: the Ottoman share of the partition includes much of Transcaucasia, which the page glosses as modern Georgia and Armenia (paraphrase); it does not mention Tbilisi or Kartli by name (confidence 2).

region.text: Kakheti, within the Transcaucasian lands of the Ottoman share

ledger.note: 1724: as for Kartli; Kakheti is not named on the page.

region.text: Isfahan and central Persia, the land Cliopatria gives the Hotaki in 1727-1733

ledger.note: 1729: the Hotaki are driven out. 'Ashraf's army was defeated in the October 1729 at the Battle of Damghan' (infobox 29 September) and 'the Hotak dynasty was eventually removed from power in Persia'; 'the Safavid restoration to the throne of Iran took place in the latter part of 1729' (Campaigns of Nader Shah page).

region.text: central Persia between Gulnabad and Isfahan

ledger.note: 1729: Hotaki rule in Persia ends (see the gain above).
1729: the court returns to Isfahan. The restoration of the Safavid throne is in the latter part of 1729; the Safavid Iran infobox keeps Isfahan as capital to 1736.

region.text: the west lands held by the Ottomans since 1724

ledger.note: 1730: the Ottoman-Persian war of 1730-1735. The war table lists 'Mahmud I vs. Nader Shah, 1730-1735'; the Tahmasp II page calls Tahmasp's own Ottoman campaign of 1731 'foolhardy'.

region.text: Tabriz, Hamadan and Kermanshah with East Azarbaijan and Ardebil

ledger.note: 12 August 1730: Nader takes Tabriz. The page has him retake Nahavand, Hamadan and then Kermanshah in 1730 and take Tabriz on 12 August 1730, after an Ottoman relief army arrived too late. Tahmasp II's failed Caucasus expedition of about 1731 ended in a treaty (undated on the page) by which he accepted Ottoman suzerainty over the Caucasus while Tabriz, Hamadan and Kermanshah were to be returned to Iran. The page names Tabriz, Hamadan and Kermanshah; East Azarbaijan and Ardebil are the provinces round Tabriz and the rest of the 1724 loss. Replaces the 1735 date of the former single event. Added after review.

region.text: the Caspian provinces of the 1723-1724 partition

ledger.note: 1732: the Treaty of Resht. The page names the 1732 Treaty of Resht and the 1735 Treaty of Ganja, and says both returned Russian-taken territory to Iran (paraphrase); which province came back under which treaty is not on the page (my reading: the southern Caspian provinces in 1732).

region.text: the Caucasian lands taken by Russia in 1723

ledger.note: 1735: the Treaty of Ganja returns the rest. See the 1732 event; the northern Caspian lands are my reading of the 1735 treaty.

region.text: the Caucasus, Ottoman since the partition of 1724

ledger.note: 1735: Iran recovers the Caucasus. The Campaigns of Nader Shah page has Shamakhi fall in August 1734, Ganja besieged and the decisive victory at Baghavard in 1735, with a peace 'securing Iranian control over the Caucasus' (the war table: Constantinople, 1736); the Treaty of Constantinople (1724) page: 'The Ottoman-Persian War (1730-35) decisively returned all Ottoman annexed territories back to Iran'. Narrowed after review: Tabriz, Hamadan and Kermanshah came back in 1730 (see the event of August 1730), not in 1735.
1735: the war of 1730-1735 ends (peace of 1735/1736).

8 March 1736: Nader Shah is crowned and the Safavid state ends. Infobox 'Disestablished: 8 March 1736'; 'Nader Shah became the official Iranian monarch in 1736' (Campaigns of Nader Shah page). The Afsharid dossier dates Nader's assembly to January 1736.

wars.name: Ottoman-Safavid War under Selim I (1505-1517)

zones.text: Tabriz, entered by Selim on 5 September 1514
Eastern Anatolia and parts of Mesopotamia

wars.outcome: Ottoman victory at Chaldiran (1514); the Ottomans enter Tabriz but leave it, and annex Eastern Anatolia and parts of Mesopotamia.
wars.note: War table: 'Selim I vs. Ismail I, 1505-1517', winner Ottoman, no treaty. Details from the Ismail I page.

wars.name: Ottoman-Safavid War (1532-1555)

zones.text: Tabriz, occupied in July 1534 and in July 1548
Baghdad, conquered peacefully by Suleiman

wars.outcome: Ottoman victory: Tahmasp recognises Ottoman sovereignty in Mesopotamia and much of Kurdistan (Peace of Amasya, June 1555); eastern Georgia stays Safavid, western Georgia goes to the Turks.
wars.note: War table: 'Suleiman I vs. Tahmasp I, 1532-1555, Amasya (1555)'. Details from the Tahmasp I page.

wars.name: Safavid-Uzbek wars of Tahmasp I (1524-1528)

zones.text: the borderlands, Astarabad, Tus and Herat

wars.outcome: The Uzbeks under Ubayd Allah Khan overrun the Khorasan borderlands (1524) and Astarabad and Tus (1528); Tahmasp wins at Jam in 1528.

wars.name: Ottoman-Safavid War (1578-1590)

zones.text: Azerbaijan, Karabagh, Shirvan, Dagestan, parts of Georgia
Tabriz

wars.outcome: Ottoman victory: the Treaty of Constantinople (1590) cedes Azerbaijan, Karabagh, Shirvan, Dagestan, parts of Georgia, Lorestan, Kurdistan and Tabriz.
wars.note: War table: 'Murad III vs. Mohammad Khodabanda / Abbas I, 1578-1590, Constantinople (1590)'. Cession list from the Abbas I page.

wars.name: Safavid-Uzbek wars of Abbas I (1589-1602)

zones.text: Herat and Mashhad
Balkh, held 1599-1602

wars.outcome: The Uzbeks take Herat (1589); Abbas retakes Mashhad (April 1598) and Herat, reaches Balkh in 1599 and loses it again in 1602.

wars.name: Ottoman-Safavid War (1603-1618)

zones.text: Tabriz, Azerbaijan and Georgia, retaken in 1603; Yerevan in June 1604
Ganja, Baku, Shirvan and Shamakhi, June 1606
Dagestan, regained with the Treaty of Nasuh Pasha of 20 November 1612

wars.outcome: Persian victory: the Treaty of Nasuh Pasha (20 November 1612) 'recognized Persian victories and restored suzerainty over most of the Caucasus'; the second phase, 1616-1618, ended with an Ottoman army of 100,000 under Halil Pasha seizing Tabriz and being ambushed near Ardabil in 1618 (Treaty of Serav, 1618, on the war table), with no border change recorded on the pages opened.
wars.note: Page: 26 September 1603 - 20 November 1612, Safavid victory; the war page itself stops at 1612 and does not mention 1616-1618 or Serav. The extension to 1618 follows the Abbas I page ('the 1603-1618 Ottoman War') and the war table of the Ottoman-Persian Wars page, which lists 'Ahmed I, Mustafa I, Osman II vs. Abbas I, 1616-1618, Serav (1618)' separately; that separate entry is merged here after review.

wars.name: Safavid suppression of the Georgian revolt (1614-1616)

zones.text: Kartli and Kakheti

wars.outcome: Iranian armies invaded Kartli and Kakheti in March 1614 and suppressed the revolt of Luarsab II and Teimuraz I; Abbas deported 30,000 Kakhetian peasants and in 1619 made Simon II the puppet ruler of Kartli.

wars.name: Safavid-Portuguese conflict in the Gulf (1602-1622)

zones.text: Bahrain, 1602
Hormuz, 1622

wars.outcome: The Portuguese lose Bahrain (1602) and, with four English ships helping Abbas, Hormuz (1622).

wars.name: Ottoman-Safavid War (1623-1639)

zones.text: Baghdad, Safavid from 14 January 1624 to December 1638
Revan, Ottoman from 8 August 1635 to spring 1636

wars.outcome: Ottoman victory: Murad IV takes Baghdad (December 1638) and the Treaty of Zuhab (17 May 1639) cedes Iraq for good and fixes the Turkey-Iran and Iraq-Iran border.

wars.name: Mughal-Safavid war (1649-1653)

zones.text: Kandahar, besieged from 28 December 1648, taken on 22 February 1649; Mughal sieges of 1651, 1652 and 1653 failed

wars.outcome: Safavid victory: Kandahar falls again to the Safavids (infobox) and on 29 September 1653 the Mughals 'finally gave up all attempts to recover Kandahar'.
wars.note: Infobox dates 28 December 1648 - 29 September 1653; the entry starts in 1648 with the siege, the contest events at the capture of 22 February 1649. Mughal attempts: 1651, Aurangzeb in 1652 (two months), Dara Shikoh in 1653 (five months). The Mughal campaign in Balkh and Badakhshan (1646-1647) is outside this war. The war of 1622-1623 for Kandahar (Mughal-Persian wars page) and the handover of 1638 are in the ledger only. Added after review.

wars.name: Hotaki invasion of Persia (1722-1729)

zones.text: central Persia

wars.outcome: Gulnabad (8 March 1722), siege of Isfahan, abdication of Soltan Hoseyn (23 October 1722); the Hotaki are beaten at Damghan in autumn 1729.

wars.name: Russian and Ottoman partition of the Safavid periphery (1722-1724)

zones.text: Derbent, Baku, Gilan, Shirvan, Mazandaran, Astarabad (Russia); the west (Ottomans)

wars.outcome: Peter the Great declares war in June 1722; the Treaty of Saint Petersburg (1723) cedes the Caspian provinces to Russia; the Treaty of Constantinople (12 June 1724) divides the periphery between Russia and the Ottomans.

wars.name: Ottoman-Persian War (1730-1735)

zones.text: the Ottoman-annexed west

wars.outcome: Persian victory: 'decisively returned all Ottoman annexed territories back to Iran'; with the Treaties of Resht (1732) and Ganja (1735) the Russian gains also return.
wars.note: War table: 'Mahmud I vs. Nader Shah, 1730-1735, Constantinople (1736), Persian'.

certainty.note: Approximate frontiers in the east, the Gulf, Georgia and the Ottoman marches; the Peace of Amasya (1555) and the Treaty of Constantinople (1590) name lands but no lines.

Sharp on the Ottoman frontier from the Treaty of Zuhab (1639), 'the western border of Iran with Iraq and Turkey' to this day; the eastern marches (Kandahar, Herat, Baluchistan) and the Gulf coast stay soft.
Collapse, occupation and partition: treaty lines of 1723, 1724, 1732 and 1735 exist, but the territory of the exiled court is not located by the pages opened.

Akbar seized Kandahar'; 'By the end of the 1603-1618 Ottoman War, Abbas had regained possession over South Caucasus and Dagestan'.

sources.title: Ottoman-Safavid War (1623-1639)
sources.note: Baghdad 1624 and 1638, Revan 1635-1636, Treaty of Zuhab 17 May 1639.

sources.title: Hotak dynasty
sources.note: Kandahar 1709, Gulnabad 8 March 1722, Isfahan 23 October 1722, Damghan 1729. Re-opened after review: silent on the Abdali seizure of Herat and Nader's capture of it.

sources.title: Tahmasp II
sources.note: Proclamation at Qazvin 10 November 1722; Treaty of Saint Petersburg 1723; deposition 1732.

sources.title: Treaty of Constantinople (1724)
sources.note: 12 June 1724 partition between the Ottomans and Russia; Resht 1732, Ganja 1735; war of 1730-1735.

sources.title: Campaigns of Nader Shah
sources.note: Restoration of 1729, Nader's crowning in 1736. Opened for Safavid end-years and the Ya'rubid Persian episode; silent on Oman. Re-opened after review for Tabriz on 12 August 1730, Herat 1729-1731 and the Caucasus in 1734-1735.

sources.title: Akbar
sources.note: Kandahar capitulates to the Mughals on 18 April 1595; opened after review.

sources.title: Mughal-Safavid war (1649-1653)
sources.note: Kandahar 1638 (Ali Mardan Khan), siege from 28 December 1648, fall on 22 February 1649, Mughal sieges 1651-1653, end 29 September 1653; opened after review.

sources.title: Mughal-Persian wars
sources.note: Siege of Kandahar from 20 May, fall on 22 June (war of 1622-1623); opened after review.

sources.title: Ottoman-Safavid War (1603-1618)
sources.note: Infobox 26 September 1603 - 20 November 1612; Tabriz October 1603, Yerevan June 1604, Ganja, Baku, Shirvan and Shamakhi June 1606, Treaty of Nasuh Pasha 20 November 1612; silent on 1616-1618; opened after review.

sources.title: Peace of Amasya
sources.note: fx-26 (F086): 1555 terms: 'Most of Iraq, including Baghdad' to the Ottomans; the frontier ran 'down the western slopes of the Zagros Mountains to the Persian Gulf'; the Ottomans keep Mesopotamia until the Treaty of Zuhab (1639).

sources.title: Battle of Chaldiran
sources.note: fx-26 (F086): 'the Ottomans annexed Eastern Anatolia and Upper Mesopotamia from Safavid Iran'; 'these areas changed hands several times over the following decades'; Kurdish chiefs switched allegiance from the Safavids to the Ottomans; the Ottoman hold was not settled until the 1555 Peace of Amasya.

sources.title: Treaty of Resht
sources.note: fx-26 (F048): signed at Rasht on 21 January 1732 by Russia and the Safavid Empire; Russia 'waived its claim to any territory south of the Kura River', which 'included return of the provinces of Gilan, Mazandaran, and Astarabad'; Derbent, Tarki and Ganja north of the Kura to return three years later (Treaty of Ganja, 1735).

sources.title: Ottoman-Safavid War (1578-1590)
sources.note: fx-26 (F086): Tabriz taken by the Ottomans in 1585 and held 'for the next two decades'; 'Cigalazade Yusuf Sinan Pasha managed to take Luristan and Hamadan' (1587); Treaty of Constantinople of 21 March 1590 cedes Azerbaijan, Karabagh, Ganja, Dagestan, Qarajadagh, parts of Georgia, Luristan and Kurdistan, with Tabriz.

notes:
Cliopatria rows: the Safavid row's last two shapes (1727-1733, 1734-1737) are slivers of 148 and 298 km2 and are marked wrong; the real realm of 1729-1736 is drawn by the Hotaki shape of 1727-1733 (not the Hotaki's own years, which end in 1729 in Persia) and by Afsharid Iran from 1734. The Hotaki dossier (hotaki-dynasty) should not draw central Persia after 1729. The shapes 1516-1533 overlap the Ottoman Empire's annexation of Eastern Anatolia; marked adjust with a minus against the Ottoman shape of 1516.

Page budget: 11 pages opened in the first run (budget 9), four more in the repair of 2026-10-25 (Akbar, Mughal-Persian wars, Mughal-Safavid war 1649-1653, Ottoman-Safavid War 1603-1618), 15 in all. The Safavid dynasty page and the Ottoman-Persian Wars page are thin on territory, so the Safavid Iran page and the Campaigns of Nader Shah page were added; the 1578-1590 war page and the Treaty of Constantinople 1590 were not opened.

Unsettled (flagged for gap-fillers):
- Kandahar (repaired after review): the Mughals took it on 18 April 1595 (Akbar page; the Abbas I page says 1590, which the Akbar page does not support), Abbas retook it on 22 June 1622 (Mughal-Persian wars page), Ali Mardan Khan handed it to Shah Jahan in 1638 and the Safavids retook it on 22 February 1649 (Mughal-Safavid war 1649-1653 page). Keyframes 1595-1612 and 1636-1648 subtract the province. On the grid the two Cliopatria shapes never overlap but split the province between them: in 1595-1625 and 1640-1647 the Mughal shape holds 152 of its 197 cells, Kandahar city included, and the Safavid shape 45; in 1626-1639 and 1648-1705 the Safavid shape holds 123 (3 of the 7 cells round the city) and the Mughal shape 74. The subtraction therefore takes 45 cells out of the Safavid shape in 1595-1625 and 1640-1647, and 123 cells in 1638-1639 and in 1648 until February 1649; the reviewer's 'drawn twice' is true of the ledger (two gains, one loss) rather than of the grid. Not entered: Humayun's Kandahar of 1545 (mughal-empire /ledger/12), the Mughal-Safavid war of 1622-1623 as a war entry.
- Repair of 2026-10-25: added the Kandahar events above, the gains of June 1606 (Ganja, Baku, Shirvan, Shamakhi) and 20 November 1612 (Dagestan, Karabakh, Lorestan, West Azarbaijan; Kurdistan is not on the page's list and is left out), the war of 1649-1653, the 1603-1618 war (the separate 1616-1618 entry is merged into it), the split of the former 1735 recovery into August 1730 (Tabriz, Hamadan, Kermanshah, East Azarbaijan, Ardebil) and 1735 (Caucasus), the Hotaki 1734 subtraction in the 1729 keyframe, counterpart 'nobody' for the 1504 gain, and month 6 for Kandahar 1622 (the Mughal-Persian wars page; the Abbas I page gives only the year). Disagreements: (a) the reviewer's text 'Herat stays with the Abdalis until 1732' is not on a page: the Campaigns of Nader Shah page has Allahyar Khan recognise Iranian suzerainty in 1729 and Herat submit in April 1731 under a treaty that left him governor, and dates neither his revolt nor the reoccupation (its only 1732 is the infobox label 'after 1732' for the Abdali commanders); Herat is therefore left inside the 1729 keyframe, where the Hotaki 1727 shape puts it and the 1734 shape does not (3 of its 203 cells). (b) The Ottoman-Safavid War (1603-1618) page covers 1603-1612 only and does not mention Serav; the extension of the war to 1618 rests on the Abbas I page and the Ottoman-Persian Wars table. (c) Karabakh is entered in 1612, not 1606, because the 1606 sentence names Ganja, Baku, Shirvan and Shamakhi only. (d) Ardebil in the August 1730 gain is not named on the Campaigns page, which names Tabriz, Hamadan and Kermanshah; it is the rest of the 1724 loss. (e) The contest of 1730-1735 keeps one zone (East Azarbaijan, Hamadan, Kermanshah, Transcaucasia) to 1735 although the first three were back by August 1730.
- Annexation of Shirvan (1538/1539): confidence 1 (Cliopatria rows only).
- The Ottoman conquest of Tabriz and Azerbaijan in the war of 1578-1590 (Tabriz fell in 1585 in other accounts) is not on any page opened; the 1590 cession is.
- 1727-1728: the pages locate only Qazvin; Tahmasp II's court and the territory it held are not drawn.
- Baghdad 1508 (Ismail I page) against 1509 (Safavid Iran page); the Safavid end 8 March 1736 (Safavid Iran page) against January 1736 (Afsharid dossier).
- Rulers: the Safavid dynasty page's reign list is followed as given (reigns share their transition year).
